content:
I want a small app for keeping track of the books I'm reading.

When I open it I want to see what I'm currently reading and what I've finished. I want to add a book from a form, mark one as finished, and click through to a book to see its title, author and my notes. I'd like to be able to send someone a link to a single book.

Nothing fancy and no accounts. Skip the database, save the books to a JSON file so they're still there after a restart.

Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). # Book tracker

A small, dependency-free app for keeping track of what you're reading.

```sh
npm start        # http://localhost:3000
npm test
```

Books are saved to `data/books.json` (created on first add), so they survive
restarts. Set `BOOKS_FILE` to store them somewhere else and `PORT` to change
the port.

## Pages

- `/` — currently reading, finished, and a form to add a book
- `/books/<id>` — a single book's title, author and notes, with a
  "Mark as finished" button and an editable notes box. This URL is shareable.

content.text:
Done. The book tracker is built, tested, and verified to survive a restart.

**To run it:** `npm start`, then open http://localhost:3000. No new dependencies were added — it uses Node's built-in `http` module and plain HTML forms.

**What you get**

- The home page shows two lists, "Currently reading" and "Finished" (most recently finished first), plus an add-book form with title, author, and notes fields.
- Each book has its own page at `/books/<id>` (an 8-character id like `/books/2f17243b`) showing the title, author, notes, and when you started or finished it. That URL is the one to send to someone. The page has a "Mark as finished" button and an editable notes box, since notes tend to accumulate as you read.
- Books are saved to `data/books.json`, created on first add. Saves write to a temp file and rename it, so a crash mid-write can't leave you with a corrupted file. `BOOKS_FILE` and `PORT` environment variables override the defaults.
- User input is HTML-escaped, empty titles/authors are rejected with a message, and unknown books return a 404.

**Files**

- `server.mjs` — starts the server
- `src/store.mjs` — loads and saves the JSON file
- `src/app.mjs` — routes and HTML
- `test/` — 16 tests (`npm test`) covering the store and every route

**Verified:** all tests pass, and I ran the real server, added two books, finished one, killed and restarted the server, and confirmed both books were still there with the right state. I deleted that sample data afterward so you start with an empty list.

One thing to decide: `data/` is not in `.gitignore`. If you'd rather your reading list not be committed with the code, add `data/` there.
